audits.text:
## 0eb83be0298d

**Classification: reproduced generator shortcut defect.** Generator SHA
`ef3101530c794a86b03f49b0aa66f3fe5ecaf7d727a101f2094198380c38160c`;
selected rule hash `4be3f14f70ed`.

The ordinary generator places only isolated, exact copies of the template in the
right board. It emits no distractor components, partial matches, overlaps, or
noise. Therefore a solver can ignore the left template entirely: split the
right board into same-color 4-connected components and mark each component's
bounding-box bottom-right corner.

I generated 20 draws per band (60 total) with the deterministic seed recipe
recorded in `checks/audit/0eb83be0298d/probe_preparation.json`, validated every
input with the target `self_check`, and applied the selected Racket rule in one
supported 60-input batch. The template-free rival matched **60/60** Racket
outputs. It then failed canonical train input 0, which also passes the target
validator: the rival misses two true matches and adds/merges component-based
markers. The exact generated witness, canonical disagreement input, Racket
output, rival output, hashes, and command are compacted in
`checks/audit/0eb83be0298d/counterexample.json`; the complete census is
`template_free_shortcut.json`.

The full audit battery independently reported **6 green, 2 advisory, 4 failed**
stages. Blocking failures were lint, defect lint, distribution, and override;
semantic contract was only advisory. These failures support, but are not needed
for, the concrete shortcut reproducer.

**Suggested repair direction, not applied:** emit target-colored and other-color
distractor components, partial/near matches, and lawful accidental adjacency;
declare the component-corner rival and require each complete lesson to refute
it. Pin `RULE_HASH`, remove fake singleton/texture controls, and make exact axes
observable.
